H1-Q1: The Visigoths were led by their Duke Fritigern. "the Visigoths, under their Duke Fritigern, fell back in dismay" [PDF p. 61].

H1-Q2: Valens required the Goths to provide hostages and surrender their arms. "if the Goth would give hostages, and surrender their arms, they should be ferried across the Danube" [PDF p. 63]. The arms condition was not met because the Goths used bribes to keep their weapons. "the bribes were accepted and the Goths retained their arms" [PDF p. 63].

H1-Q3: Lupicinus withheld food to fill his own pockets and sold provisions at exorbitant prices. "the governor, Lupicinus, to fill his own pockets, held back the food, and doled out what he chose to give at exorbitant prices" [PDF p. 63].

H1-Q4: The battle at Ad Salices thinned the ranks of both sides but did not produce a decisive result. "A desperate pitched battle at Ad Salices... thinned the ranks of both sides, but led to no decisive result" [PDF p. 64].

H1-Q5: Not stated in the supplied passage.
